info.title: Telplin generates signature files for F#.

options.name: --files
options.description:
Process only these files of the project. Every source file
is processed when this is not given.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Print the signatures to the console and write nothing.

options.name: --record
options.description:
Also save the compiler arguments of the design time build
next to the project, as a .rsp file. Passing that file as the
input later skips the build.

options.name: --only-record
options.description:
Save the compiler arguments as with --record, and stop there.
No signature is generated.

options.name: --include-private-bindings
options.description: Include private bindings in the signature file.

options.name: --keep-unused
options.description:
Keep let bindings that no other file of this project uses.
By default they are left out of the signature, which makes
them private. Only this project is looked at: a binding used
by another project, by tests, through reflection or by
consumers of a published library is not seen, so use this
for a public API. Types, members and bindings with an
attribute are always kept.

options.name: --no-verify
options.description:
Skip the check that the project still compiles with the new
signatures in place. Files are written without it.

options.name: --no-project
options.description:
Do not list the signature files in the project file. By
default each one is added directly before its implementation
file, when the input is a project.

options.name: --keep-private
options.description:
Leave the private keyword on let bindings in the implementation
file. By default it is removed from the bindings the signature
leaves out, since the signature is what makes them private.

options.name: --force
options.description:
Write the signatures even when that check fails.
For debugging purposes only.

options.name: --help
options.description:
Display this page and exit.
Input:
A project file (.fsproj), a folder holding exactly one, a source file (.fs), or a
response file (.rsp). A source file stands for the nearest project above it that
has it as a Compile item, and is the one file processed. A project is built first,
a design time build that asks MSBuild for the compiler arguments; anything after
-- is passed to that build. A response file holds those arguments as saved by
--record and skips the build. Signature files are written next to the source
files, as .fsi.
Learn more about Telplin:   https://nojaf.com/telplin/docs/
Try it online:              https://nojaf.com/telplin/
Report an issue:            https://github.com/nojaf/telplin/issues
